乙酉.work: You suit work that needs precision and standards, such as design, beauty, clerical work, or quality control, where you can make good work within limited conditions. Don't stay silent just because the environment has many restrictions. Speak up when you need something.
乙酉.watch: You may keep pressure inside while looking fine on the surface. When you're tired, take a walk and spend time in nature. It loosens your heart and gives your mind a change of scene.
乙酉.ask_next: The thing that makes me feel boxed in right now: is there any room to adjust it?

甲午.title: A big tree standing in the noon sun
甲午.plain: Jia Wood is a big tree growing upward, and Wu is the hottest stretch of a summer noon. The tree gleams in the sun, its leaves sending water out all the while. You come across as generous and outspoken, and when you have an idea you want people to know it. Often you're the one who warms up the room. But the noon sun doesn't stay overhead forever. Your enthusiasm comes fast and gets used up fast. You feel best when you have something worth throwing yourself into, where your talent has room to work, and when you know to find a patch of shade for yourself while the sun is strongest.
甲午.love: When you like someone, you're clearly good to them: quick replies, plenty to say. If the other person warms up slowly, you may feel you're the only one invested. Try slowing your pace a half beat and leave them room to come toward you.
甲午.work: You suit roles that call for expression, creativity, or lifting the mood, such as planning, teaching, or sales. You have plenty of ideas and charge hard at the start, but you're more likely to lose patience midway. A partner who can help you finish will make things much easier.
甲午.watch: You speak fast, and sometimes your words come out sharper than you meant. When emotions rise, pause for three seconds and ask whether this sentence is meant to solve the problem or just to win.
甲午.ask_next: The thing that has you burning brightest lately: is it what you truly want, or are you being pushed along by expectations?

乙未.title: A vine climbing a field ridge in late summer
乙未.plain: Picture a soft vine. That's Yi Wood, and that's you. Wei beneath your feet is the tail end of summer, farmland baked a little dry. Plants on dry fields look unremarkable, yet their roots hold on tight. The more ordinary the conditions, the better they are at finding a crack to live in. You seem gentle and easygoing, but you're tough underneath, and once you've decided on something you'll quietly keep at it for a long time. You're also nostalgic, and find it hard to let go of family, old friends, and familiar places. Your steadiness is very reliable, though sometimes you swallow your hardships, and others can't tell you're tired too.
乙未.love: In relationships you're the one who takes care of people. You remember your partner's habits and are willing to adapt. But you rarely say what you want, and the hurt builds up until it bursts out. Try voicing small needs earlier.
乙未.work: You suit work that needs patience and long-term care, such as administration, customer service, farm products, or a handmade brand. You don't like the spotlight, but what's handed to you gets done steadily, and managers usually trust you more over time. Remember to keep a record of your own contributions.
乙未.watch: You tend to look after others first and put yourself last. When you're tired, saying "I need a rest" isn't selfish. It's caring for the roots of your vine.
乙未.ask_next: Is there something you've been quietly holding up that you'd actually like to share with someone?

丙申.title: Sun shining on an autumn mountain road
丙申.plain: Bing Fire is the sun, and Shen is early autumn, a place with a metallic edge that also carries a sense of roads and movement. The sun shines on a mountain road stretching into the distance, bright and open, always wanting to see what's ahead. Your mind turns fast and you're very curious. You like new places, new friends, and new ideas, and you're easily noticed in a crowd. The downside is that with so many interests you often start several roads at once and aren't sure which one to follow to the end. What you need isn't less enthusiasm, but a way to pick the one road you most want to take.
丙申.love: You're drawn to people who are fun and easy to talk to. You're very charming in the early, undefined stage, but once the heat fades you can get distracted. If the other person needs a sense of security, use your actions to show you're still here and still want to walk together.
丙申.work: You suit work that involves movement and frequent contact with people or information, such as marketing, sales, travel, or media. You're good at finding new openings, but watch out for promising too much. Pick one or two things each quarter to go deep on, and the results will be easier to see.
丙申.watch: Starting too many things at once can leave them stalled halfway. Before you begin, ask yourself: will I still care about this in three months? If not, set it aside for now.
丙申.ask_next: Of the roads in front of you now, if you could only take one first, which would you choose?

丁酉.title: Candlelight on a box of delicate jewelry
丁酉.plain: Think of yourself as a candle or a desk lamp. That's Ding Fire: the light isn't big, but it shows what's near very clearly. You is autumn's harvest, a place with a metallic shine, like a box of jewelry. Candlelight on jewelry makes every detail sparkle. You're sharp about beauty and quality, you look closely when choosing things or reading people, and you know how to give your days some flavor. You don't like loud show, but you put care into small things, and the people around you feel it. Still, your standards for detail can turn into being hard on yourself, and a small flaw may stay on your mind for a long time.
丁酉.love: You show love through small things, like remembering something your partner mentioned in passing. You want to be treated with the same care, and when they're careless you're disappointed but say nothing. Saying directly what matters to you works better than making them guess.
丁酉.work: You suit work that values quality and detail, such as design, editing, finance, jewelry, or beauty. You spot problems others miss and are good at quality control. Just don't polish everything to perfection before handing it in. Delivering at eighty percent is fine.
丁酉.watch: You're too strict with yourself and replay small mistakes. When you finish something, first note three things you did well, then look at what to change.
丁酉.ask_next: That small flaw you can't let go of lately: does it really matter that much?

戊戌.title: A mountain stacked on a high mountain
戊戌.plain: Wu Earth is a mountain, and Xu is late autumn, dry and thick earth, like a plateau on a summit. Mountain upon mountain, tall and steady, very hard to move. You have principles and do what you say, you don't change your stance easily, and in big matters you stay remarkably calm. People around you often treat you as their backing. Standing high, you're used to carrying things alone and rarely ask for help, which can make you seem hard to approach. Your steadiness is a great strength. Just let others climb up to see you now and then, so you don't have to guard everything alone.
戊戌.love: You're serious about love. You don't start easily, but once you do, you're devoted. You express yourself in a reserved way, often doing instead of saying. If the other person needs to hear a few words, try saying what you feel. It won't cost you face.
戊戌.work: You suit roles that carry responsibility and decisions, such as management, engineering, real estate, or public service. You can last through long projects and hold a room steady. Watch out for sticking too hard to your own way, and listen to the newer methods of younger colleagues.
戊戌.watch: When you're too stubborn, even good intentions can sound like orders. Starting with "What do you think?" often makes things easier to discuss, and the other person is more willing to cooperate.
戊戌.ask_next: Is there something you could actually let someone else try?

己亥.title: A moist field by the river
己亥.plain: You're a field that can be farmed, which is Ji Earth. Hai, where you sit, is early-winter water, like a river or lake. A field beside water is soft and damp, and anything can grow in it, but the water can also carry some of it away. You're gentle and accepting, you sense other people's feelings well, and you can take in anyone who comes to you with troubles. Your head is full of ideas, and you're good at planning the small details of life. But your boundaries are a bit loose. Other people's emotions and demands flow in, and you often take them all on, until your own field is soaked. Building a small ridge around your heart is a practice you really need.
己亥.love: You're very considerate in relationships and willing to accommodate. Afraid of upsetting the other person, you may step back so often that you can't say what you want anymore. Work out your own bottom line first, and then talking about compromise will feel more solid.
己亥.work: You suit work that looks after people or pulls resources together, such as HR, social work, food service, or administration. You get along well and communicate easily, so people often ask you for favors. Practice turning down work that isn't yours, and keep your time for what truly matters.
己亥.watch: You're so easygoing that you can get swamped by other people's business. Before agreeing, say "Let me think about it," give yourself a little time, and reply once you're clear.
己亥.ask_next: Lately, what is something you didn't really want to agree to but agreed to anyway?

庚子.title: A knife soaking in winter river water
庚子.plain: Geng Metal is a knife or a piece of iron, and Zi is the water of deep winter. Iron dipped in an icy river gets washed bright and sharp, and its reflection comes out clear. Your mind is clear and quick. You see the key point of a matter at a glance, speak directly, and don't like talking around things. You have a strong sense of justice and will speak up about what you can't stand to see. This sharpness makes you good at solving problems, but it can also come across as cold. You care about people deeply; you're just used to giving reasons before feelings. Switch the order, and people will understand you better.
庚子.love: In love you are honest and don't enjoy mind-reading games. But if you point out your partner's flaws too quickly, they may feel inspected. Listen to everything they want to say first, then share your view, and the relationship will soften a lot.
庚子.work: You suit work that calls for judgment, analysis or technical skill, such as engineering, paralegal work, research or quality control. You are good at spotting gaps and you work efficiently. On a team, remember to give others more recognition, and your suggestions will be easier to accept.
庚子.watch: Your words can land like a blade and easily hurt the people you care about. Before saying something harsh, ask yourself: am I trying to help, or trying to prove I'm right?
庚子.ask_next: The thing you haven't said lately: if you said it at a different temperature, what would it sound like?

辛丑.title: A gem buried in cold winter soil
辛丑.plain: There is a gem, Xin Metal, buried in Chou, the coldest, dampest, most frozen soil of winter. A gem in the earth doesn't show from the outside, yet it stays well protected until the time comes to be dug out. You come across as low-key and steady, in no hurry to show off, though inside you have your own ideas and taste. You warm up slowly, move carefully step by step, and rarely act on impulse. This patience is your foundation. But sometimes you hide too deeply, and good things go unseen, so you miss the chance to be noticed.
辛丑.love: In love you are cautious and need a long time of watching before you trust someone with your heart. Once you're sure, you give a lot quietly. Your partner may not be able to read your calm, so saying now and then that you miss them can put them at ease.
辛丑.work: You suit work that builds up over time, such as accounting, research, technical work, or fields related to collecting and preservation. You can stand repetition and hold on to the details. Remember to share your results when the time is right, rather than finishing and tucking them away in a drawer.
辛丑.watch: You think about everything too long before moving, and may miss the right moment. Give yourself a deadline, and when time is up, take one small step first. The way becomes clear only once you walk it.
辛丑.ask_next: What good thing do you have in your hands that you still haven't shown anyone?

壬寅.title: A great river flowing through a spring forest
壬寅.plain: Ren Water is a great river, and Yin is early spring, when trees are just about to bud. The river runs through the forest, watering the new trees along the way and carrying itself farther on. You are open-hearted, like learning new things and meeting new people, and you're full of curiosity about the world. You take good care of others and are glad to share what you know, often the idea person in your circle of friends. But rivers don't like to stop. You tire quickly of unchanging days and your passions switch fast, so you need to learn to let one thing grow slowly.
壬寅.love: In love you are generous and easy to be with, and you take your partner to many new places. But you need freedom, and being held too tightly makes you want to run. Agreeing on each other's space is much better than quietly pulling away, and it reassures your partner too.
壬寅.work: You suit teaching, publishing, travel, creative work, or work that opens up new markets. You're good at guiding newcomers and at making complicated things simple. When choosing a job, look for room to grow. That is the key to your staying long.
壬寅.watch: You have many ideas and move fast, so you can end up doing a little of this and a little of that. Each day before you finish, take five minutes to see which thing really moved forward today.
壬寅.ask_next: If you were given a whole year to focus on growing just one tree, what would you plant?

癸卯.title: Fine rain falling on a spring meadow
癸卯.plain: Spring's fine rain is Gui Water, and Mao is mid-spring, when plants are at their most lush. Fine rain falls on the meadow quietly, yet a whole expanse of green grows from it. You are delicate and sensitive, attuned to the mood of a room and to other people's feelings, and often understand with just a glance. You have an artistic side, love words, music and beautiful things, and keep a little world of your own. Your gentleness nourishes the people around you. But when it rains too much, you can give away all your strength and forget that you need care too.
癸卯.love: In love you are gentle and considerate, and good at reading your partner's mood. Because you're so sensitive, a little coolness from them can set you thinking a lot. Rather than guessing over and over in your head, ask lightly, "Are you doing okay today?"
癸卯.work: You suit work that needs sensitivity and communication, such as design, writing, counseling, education, or anything related to aesthetics. You notice well how users or clients feel. Watch out for caring too much about others' opinions, which can cloud your judgment.
癸卯.watch: Your mood is easily carried along by other people. When you feel drained, step out of that setting for a while, let your own rain pause, and then decide whether to go back.
癸卯.ask_next: Lately, who have you given your gentleness to, and who is looking after your feelings?

甲辰.title: A great tree with roots sunk into moist, rich soil
甲辰.plain: Jia Wood is a big tree, and Chen is late spring, damp soil carrying moisture. Roots sunk into fertile earth can drink water and stand firm, so the tree grows tall and straight. You are ambitious and want to do big things, and you also have the stamina to bring plans down to earth. You work with a plan, like to hold the whole picture, and on a team you often become the one who makes the decisions without trying. Your foundation is thick, so change doesn't easily knock you down. What to practice is softening a little: don't keep everything in your own hands, and give others a chance to grow with you.
甲辰.love: In love you are reliable and responsible, and you think about the future for both of you. But sometimes you're too rational, used to planning and forgetting romance. Now and then, put the plan aside and do something with your partner that has no purpose.
甲辰.work: You suit work that needs coordination, planning and long-term running, such as management, construction, financial planning or starting a business. You can handle pressure and carry responsibility. Remember to delegate. You don't need to do every detail yourself.
甲辰.watch: When you want to control too much, the pressure keeps piling up. Each week, list one thing you can hand off. Practice letting go, and give others a chance to grow.
甲辰.ask_next: Of everything you're carrying now, which one thing could you actually hand to someone else?

乙巳.title: A flower blooming in early summer sunlight
乙巳.plain: Early summer sunlight gets stronger by the day. That is Si, and you are a flower in its light, Yi Wood. In early summer, as the sun grows stronger, a flower lit by it blooms beautifully and its scent travels far. You are outgoing and eloquent, express yourself well, and know how to dress and shape your image. You're quick and full of ideas, and people often remember you the moment you speak. But when the sun is too fierce, a flower can dry out. You shine in front of others, yet in private you're often worn out and need time alone to restore your moisture. For a flower to bloom long, its roots must reach water too.
乙巳.love: In love you are very charming and know how to create surprise and romance. You need to feel appreciated, and if your partner responds too little, you feel you're performing a solo act. Say how you want to be treated, and it will be easier for them to meet you.
乙巳.work: You suit work in performance, creativity and communication, such as marketing, hosting, design, public relations or the beauty industry. You're good at packaging ideas attractively. Watch for saying more than you do, and remember to turn your bright moments into results.
乙巳.watch: Caring too much about how others see you can wear you out. Each week, set aside a stretch of time when no one is watching and do only what makes you happy, with no photos and no sharing.
乙巳.ask_next: If no one were watching, what would you most want to spend your time on?

丙午.title: The noon sun hanging at its highest point
丙午.plain: Bing Fire is the sun, and Wu is the time of day when the sun is highest and hottest. The noon sun shines strongest and most directly, and everyone can see it. You are passionate, frank and action-oriented. You do what you think of and dislike dragging things out. You are contagious, lifting the mood wherever you go, and loyal, always first to rush in when a friend is in trouble. This warmth is your greatest asset. But when fire is too strong, it can turn impatient, wanting to push straight through at the first snag, and you can burn yourself out in the busyness, forgetting that rest is a kind of strength too.
丙午.love: In love you are passionate and direct. If you like someone, you say so, and you don't play hard to get. But you're hasty, and you get impatient when your partner replies slowly. Learn to wait a little and let the warmth travel over slowly, and the relationship will last longer.
丙午.work: You suit work that needs drive and taking the lead, such as sales, starting a business, events, sports-related work or leadership roles. You act fast and dare to decide. Watch for rushing too hard toward results, and remember to leave time for details and communication.
丙午.watch: Your temper comes quickly, and when you're in a hurry you say harsh things. When you notice your voice getting loud, drink some water and walk a lap away from your seat before coming back. The words will come out much easier.
丙午.ask_next: The result you've been eager for lately: what would happen if it came a little slower?

丁未.title: Lamplight shining over a summer night field
丁未.plain: A lamp in a summer-night field is what Ding Fire looks like; Wei is late summer, ground warmed by the sun. Lamplight over a summer-night field isn't glaring, yet it puts people at ease. You're gentle and loyal, devoted to home, and you look after the people around you. You're often the lamp in everyone's heart. You're patient in your work and like to make your days warm and comfortable. You have plenty of ideas inside; you just don't show them off. Watch out for shining so hard on others that you only notice your own lamp oil is nearly gone when it's already low. Lighting it again then is hard work.
丁未.love: In love you're careful and gentle. You keep your partner's tastes in mind and care a lot about the feeling of home. Sometimes you hide your complaints to keep the peace. Mention small things while they're small, before they pile up into a mountain.
丁未.work: You suit caring or service work, or work that needs long-term tending, such as food service, education, nursing administration, or community work. You help a team hold together. Remember to ask for the resources and recognition you've earned, too.
丁未.watch: You often put yourself second for the sake of the bigger picture. Once a week, ask yourself: do I truly want to do this, or am I just too shy to say no? The answer will show you your next step.
丁未.ask_next: The people around you are all cared for by you. How would you like to be cared for?

甲寅.plain: Jia Wood is a big tree, and Yin is early spring, when trees are in full growth. This tree stands in its own forest, with deep roots and straight branches, and it needs no one to prop it up. You are independent and principled, with a clear sense of direction, and you don't much like being told what to do. You are upright and driven. What you set out to do keeps growing upward, and you look after the friends around you. But a tree that grows very straight doesn't bend easily. When opinions differ you hold firm, and you can clash with others who are just as strong-minded. Learn to bend a little when the wind comes, and the tree stands longer.
甲寅.love: In love you are sincere. If you like someone, you say so, and you respect their space. You need respect too, and if too much is asked of you, you want to pull back. When you disagree, try first to understand where the other person is coming from.
甲寅.work: You suit work that calls for independence and starting new things, such as launching a business, planning, education, or technical development. You are good at leading the way on something new and don't like going in circles inside a framework. What to practice is cooperation: share the credit with the people who worked alongside you.
甲寅.watch: You want to rely on yourself so much that you may turn down help. Next time someone reaches out a hand, try saying "Yes, thank you." It won't make you weaker.
甲寅.ask_next: Is there something you've been pushing through alone lately? Who could you ask to do it with you?
甲寅.title: The straightest tree in the forest

乙卯.title: Spring grass covering the whole hillside
乙卯.plain: You are like flowers and vines, which is Yi Wood. The Mao you sit on is mid-spring, when plants are at their lushest. Spring grass covers the whole slope, soft yet nearly impossible to pull out completely, growing into every gap. You are friendly and easy to be around, good with people, well liked, and adaptable. You seem easygoing, but you have your own ideas, and what you want to do you will get done, even if you take a detour. You value freedom and don't like being tied down. Watch out for caring so much about everyone's feelings that your own direction starts to sway, and you end up busy all around without knowing where you're headed.
乙卯.love: In love you are gentle and romantic, and good at setting the mood. You have many friends, so your partner may feel insecure. Let them know your circle, and let them feel they are the special one, and a sense of security will grow slowly.
乙卯.work: You suit work that involves people and flexibility, such as public relations, marketing, aesthetics, teaching, and client care. You are good at connecting people. Watch out for trying to please everyone and ending up unable to finish your own work.
乙卯.watch: You care so much about everyone's reaction that your decisions can go back and forth. Write down what you really want first, then listen to others' opinions, and your mind will feel steadier.
乙卯.ask_next: If you didn't have to worry about anyone's opinion, what decision would you most want to make?

丙辰.title: Morning light on a misty field
丙辰.plain: Bing Fire is the sun, and Chen is late spring, with damp, fertile soil. Sunlight falls warmly on a misty field, and everything in the soil grows well. You are generous and warm-hearted, happy to share, and you like making the people around you happy. You have plenty of creativity and know how to turn an idea into something everyone can join in. You are kind to others, don't keep score, and are often the life of your circle of friends. But you give too easily, often thinking more of others than of yourself, and you take on more than you can carry, until you have no time left for yourself.
丙辰.love: In love you are warm and generous, and you like planning things for your partner and creating happy moments. You hope for an equally warm response, and you feel let down when they are too cool. Say what kind of response you need.
丙辰.work: You suit work that involves creativity, sharing, and service, such as education, food and drink, events, content creation, and public welfare. You bring warmth to a team. Watch out for being too agreeable. Politely hand back what isn't yours to do.
丙辰.watch: When you give a lot but feel awkward asking for anything, you can feel things are out of balance. Before you give to others, check that you still have energy to spare. Giving within your means is a kind of thoughtfulness too.
丙辰.ask_next: You've done a lot for others lately. What would you like to do for yourself?

丁巳.title: A candle flame beside the stove fire before noon
丁巳.plain: A single candle flame is Ding Fire, and Si is early summer, when fire energy is growing strong. A candle set beside a stove fire, the two flames reflecting each other, burn brighter and brighter. You are passionate and perceptive, with strong inner drive, and very focused when you get serious. Your intuition is good, and your first impression often catches the key point. You like to express yourself and to be seen. Your fire can warm people and light the place you want to go. But when the fire is too strong, your moods swing: full of passion one moment, very tired the next, like a flame the wind keeps making bigger and smaller.
丁巳.love: In love you are devoted and love with full attention, and you care a lot about how your partner responds. When you heat up, you can overthink and rush. Slow the pace and give the relationship time to warm gradually, and your partner will feel more at ease coming closer.
丁巳.work: You suit work that calls for focus and passion, such as research, creative work, performance, technical work, and professional consulting. Once you commit, you go deep. Watch how you spread your heat, and save your energy for the moments that really matter.
丁巳.watch: Once your emotions rise, they are hard to stop, and you can wear yourself out. When you notice you're too wound up or too low, return first to a regular daily routine.
丁巳.ask_next: What is the one thing you most want to put your passion into right now?

戊午.title: A great mountain warmed by the sun
戊午.plain: Wu Earth is a mountain, and Wu the branch is midday in summer. The mountain, warmed by the noon sun, looks steady outside but holds heat inside. You come across as reliable and weighty, and people like to talk things over with you. Inside, you actually have a lot of passion and ambition, and once you are sure, you give it everything. You care about face and keep your word. But the heat stays trapped in the mountain. You rarely talk about your stress, and if you hold on too long, your temper may flare suddenly and surprise even you. Give the heat somewhere to go, and the mountain stays steady.
戊午.love: In love you are steady and responsible, and you give your partner a lot of security. You speak quite directly, which can sometimes come across as forceful. When your partner shares what's on their mind, listen first, and don't rush to offer solutions.
戊午.work: You suit work that calls for stability and leadership, such as management, real estate, construction, public service, and team lead roles. You can carry the big picture. Watch out for caring too much about face. Asking for help early on a problem is better than pushing through alone.
戊午.watch: When you keep stress bottled up, it can burst out suddenly. Each week, find a way to let the heat out, such as exercise, a walk, or a talk with a friend.
戊午.ask_next: Who would you most like to tell about the pressure you've been keeping inside lately?

己未.title: Two connected fields in late summer
己未.plain: You are a field, Ji Earth. The Wei you sit on is also dry, warm late-summer earth, so field joins field into one thick stretch of land. You are practical and grounded, value a settled life, and do things step by step, rarely taking risks. You are sentimental, with deep feelings for family, familiar people, and familiar places, and you hold on well to what is yours. You look gentle, but inside you have firm opinions and are not easily persuaded. This stubbornness makes you reliable, but when you hold too tightly to your own way, a new opportunity may come close, and while you're still wondering whether to open the door, it has already moved on.
己未.love: In love you are faithful and take commitment seriously, and you like a steady, long-flowing relationship. You aren't one for sweet words and tend to show care instead of saying it. When your partner needs something fresh, try going somewhere new together.
己未.work: You suit work that calls for stability and patience, such as administration, finance, agriculture, real estate, and long-term client care. You are dependable and put people at ease. Watch out for fearing change too much, and now and then try a new tool or method.
己未.watch: When you hold too tightly to the old ways, you can miss new opportunities. When something is unfamiliar, don't say no right away. Give it one small try, and decide after you've tried it.
己未.ask_next: Is there something new you've wanted to try but never started?

庚申.title: Two freshly sharpened knives lying side by side
庚申.plain: Geng Metal is a piece of iron or a blade, and Shen is early autumn, when Metal energy is strong. Iron meets iron, like two freshly sharpened knives side by side, sharp and clean. You are decisive and quick to act. Once you see clearly, you do it, and you don't like dragging things out. You are very competitive, you get more energized the bigger the challenge, and you are loyal to your friends. Your efficiency is admirable. But when the blade is too sharp, your words and decisions can be too hard, and when you meet someone as strong as you, neither of you gives way and things get stuck. Knowing how to sheathe the blade is rarer than knowing how to draw it.
庚申.love: In love you are direct and clear. If you like someone, you go after them, and if you don't, you say so plainly. But you value efficiency so much that you may not give the companionship and patience your partner needs. Slow down and listen to how they feel.
庚申.work: You suit work that calls for decisiveness and speed, such as sales, engineering, technical work, highly competitive fields, and starting a business. You dare to charge ahead. Watch out for friction with coworkers. Set the rules clearly before dividing up the work.
庚申.watch: When you're very competitive, you can turn cooperation into a contest. When you notice you're fighting over who wins, ask first: what is this meant to achieve in the end?
庚申.ask_next: Who have you been competing with lately, and is that contest really worth winning?

辛酉.title: A whole box of shining jewelry
辛酉.plain: The time in autumn when Metal energy is purest is called You, and you are one of its gems: Xin Metal. Picture a gem in a whole box of jewelry, where every piece is clean, bright, and well made. You care about taste and quality. You hold high standards for yourself and the things around you, and you work with care and precision. You have strong self-respect and clear principles, and you don't compromise easily. You have a good eye and can often pick out the best. But when your standards run too high, everything shows a flaw, and you often feel you aren't good enough yourself. Allow a little imperfection, and your light will feel more at ease.
辛酉.love: In love, you are picky but devoted. You only commit once you find someone you truly admire. You notice details, and you get disappointed when a partner is careless. Try saying your expectations out loud, and give the other person a little room to make mistakes.
辛酉.work: You suit work that needs precision and quality, such as jewelry, design, precision technical work, accounting, and quality control. Your work is fine and holds up well to a close look. Watch for chasing perfection too far, and remember that time is part of quality too.
辛酉.watch: Being too hard on others and yourself can make relationships tense. Each day, find one thing someone did well and say so out loud. Relationships will slowly loosen up.
辛酉.ask_next: Where have you been hardest on yourself lately, and could you ease up a little?

戊申.title: Hidden in the great mountain, roads that lead in every direction
戊申.plain: Wu Earth is a mountain, and Shen is early autumn, a place with the feel of metal and roads. A mountain holds ore and paths; it looks heavy, but it opens in every direction. You seem steady outside and are very flexible inside. Your mind moves fast, and you're good at finding ways and resources. You're practical and like to turn ideas into results you can see, and you can often find another way through a difficulty. You don't care for empty talk, and you work efficiently. But your ideas change quickly, which can leave people around you behind, and you may take on too much at once and pack your schedule full.
戊申.love: In love you're practical and show care through action, like solving problems or arranging daily life. But when you're busy, you can overlook your partner's feelings. Now and then, stop and listen without rushing to give an answer.
戊申.work: You suit work that needs problem-solving and follow-through, such as engineering, logistics, technical work, business development, or project management. You adapt well and can carry practical work. Be careful not to take on too many projects, and save your best quality for what matters most.
戊申.watch: When you rush to solve things, you may forget to ask first what the other person wants. Confirming the goal before you start saves a lot of redoing and cuts down on misunderstandings.
戊申.ask_next: Of everything on your plate right now, which one do you most want to do as well as you possibly can?

己酉.title: A field carefully tended in harvest season
己酉.plain: Autumn harvest time is You, and you are the field, Ji Earth. Carefully tended through autumn, the field bears cluster after cluster of fruit. You work with care and have clever hands. You like to make things with finesse and know the small pleasures of life. You have your own taste and methods, and you often quietly get things done beautifully. You speak gently but with insight, and you're easy to talk to once people know you. Watch out for holding yourself to a high standard. You often feel it isn't good enough yet and hesitate to show it, so good fruit stays on the branch.
己酉.love: In love you're thoughtful and attentive to detail, and you remember your partner's little habits. You also hope they appreciate your effort, and you feel low when it goes unnoticed. Saying what you've done isn't taking credit.
己酉.work: You suit work that needs craft, detail, and planning, such as design, baking, handmade goods, editing, or accounting. Your work holds up under a close look. What to practice is trusting yourself: name your price boldly and show your work openly.
己酉.watch: Caring too much about perfection makes you put off handing things in. Tell yourself, "Finish first, then revise." Put out a first version, and feedback will help you refine it.
己酉.ask_next: That piece you keep refining: when could you let people see it, even as it is?

庚戌.title: An iron blade resting beside a thick city wall
庚戌.plain: Geng Metal is a piece of iron or a weapon, and Xu is late autumn, dry, heavy earth, like a city wall or fortress. Iron beside a wall can hold its ground and is ready to set out at any time. You're strong-willed and principled, loyal to your friends, and hard to move once you've decided. Under pressure you can bear a lot, and you have a refusal-to-give-in drive. You often step forward when others hold back. Your directness makes you seem dependable, but it can also make people feel distance. Inside you care deeply; your shell is just harder. If you let people see your soft side, you'll gain many more true friends.
庚戌.love: In love you're loyal and responsible, and you follow through on what you promise. You show love in a firm way, helping with things more than saying sweet words. Once in a while, soften your tone and say a caring word, and your partner will really appreciate it.
庚戌.work: You suit work that needs boldness and follow-through, such as management, engineering, disciplined services, starting a business, or technical roles. You dare to make the call and hold your bottom line. Leaving a little more flexibility in teamwork will win more support for your decisions.
庚戌.watch: Holding too firmly to your own sense of right and wrong can lead to head-on clashes. In a dispute, first find one point you agree on, then discuss the differences, and the mood will ease a lot.
庚戌.ask_next: For the thing you've been insisting on lately, is there another way to reach the same goal?

辛亥.title: A gem washed in clear water
辛亥.plain: Clear water of early winter is Hai, and you are a gem washed by it, Xin Metal. A gem washed in clear water shines clean, and stands out. You're smart and quick, and you express yourself well, often saying precisely what everyone wanted to say but didn't. You value cleanness and sharpness, hold standards for beauty and quality, and have strong opinions. Your talent is easy to notice, but when your words are too polished or too fast, they may sting someone without you realizing. Your light is bright. Soften it a little and it will reach more people.
辛亥.love: In love you're romantic and picky. You like a relationship with quality and care how your partner speaks. You talk well, but you're quick-tongued in arguments. When tempers run hot, don't reply to messages yet. Talking once you're calm leaves fewer regrets.
辛亥.work: You suit work that needs eloquence, creativity, and judgment, such as writing, design, consulting, teaching, or media. Your ideas are fresh and you express them well. Take care not to stop at thinking; pick one direction and keep producing work.
辛亥.watch: Your mouth moves faster than your heart, and one joke may be remembered for a long time. Before speaking, ask yourself: will this feel okay to the other person? It's never too late to think first.
辛亥.ask_next: Is there something you've said beautifully but haven't actually done yet?

壬子.title: The great sea flowing deep on a winter night
壬子.plain: Ren Water is rivers and seas, and Zi is the water of deep winter. Water upon water is like a bottomless sea on a winter night: quiet on the surface, with a strong current below. You're smart and independent-minded, think deeply and far, and often have your own take on things. You're independent, dislike being managed, and need a lot of space. You adapt well to your surroundings and even gain energy from change. But with so much water, your worries sit deep, others find you hard to read, and you may stew alone too long, making simple things seem complicated.
壬子.love: In love you're charming and you need freedom. You have many thoughts about love but don't always say them, so your partner may feel they can't quite reach you. Sharing what's on your mind now and then will bring you closer.
壬子.work: You suit work that needs strategy, flexibility, and quick response, such as trade, logistics, research, consulting, or freelancing. You see far and spot opportunities well. Watch out for carrying too much alone, and learn to find partners you can trust.
壬子.watch: Thinking too much without speaking can trap you in a dead end. When something is stuck in your mind, tell someone you trust, or even just write it down.
壬子.ask_next: The thing you keep turning over in your mind lately: who would you most like to talk to about it?

癸丑.title: Winter rain falling on a frosted field
癸丑.plain: For Gui Chou, picture winter rain: Gui Water is rain, and Chou is the coldest earth, damp and frozen. Winter rain on a frosted field looks bleak, yet it's quietly nourishing next spring's soil. You're calm and reserved with great endurance, and you rarely complain in hard times; you quietly get through. You think deeply, often form your own judgments, and aren't easily persuaded. Your resilience is admirable, but you tend to tuck stress inside. Outside you seem fine while inside it weighs heavily, and it needs an outlet. Find someone you feel safe talking to, and winter won't be so cold.
癸丑.love: In love you warm up slowly and take a long time to give your whole heart, but once you've decided, you stay devoted. You rarely mention hardship, so your partner may not know you need support. Try saying "I'm a bit tired today" to give them a chance to come closer.
癸丑.work: You suit work that needs endurance and built-up expertise, such as research, finance, technical work, records management, or long-term projects. You can bear quiet stretches and keep progress on track. Remember to schedule rest for yourself rather than always pushing through.
癸丑.watch: Tucking all your stress inside leaves body and mind tense over time. Set aside some time each day to zone out and slow your pace, so you don't have to stay tight every moment.
癸丑.ask_next: For the thing you've been quietly holding up, what kind of support do you need most right now?

壬戌.title: A great river held steady by its banks
壬戌.plain: Ren Water is a great river, and Xu is dry, thick Earth at the end of autumn, like an embankment. The river is held in by its banks. The water is powerful, yet there is a boundary that keeps it from running wild. You are ambitious and bold, you think far ahead, and you dare to take on big things. You look calm on the outside, but inside you carry many thoughts and a lot of pressure, and you often feel you have to shoulder something. You do well within rules and know how to perform under pressure. But when a river is held back too long, feelings get bottled up. They pile up until they burst out all at once, and even you can't hold them back.
壬戌.love: In love, you are dependable and think a lot on your partner's behalf. But you rarely talk about your own pressure, so the other person may feel you are far away. Share a little of what's weighing on you, and they will understand better how to be there for you.
壬戌.work: You suit work that needs strategy and resilience under pressure, such as management, finance-related administration, logistics, consulting, and public-sector jobs. You can actually do your best under pressure. Watch for keeping going nonstop, and give yourself a regular rhythm of rest.
壬戌.watch: Pressure held in for too long can lead to a sudden outburst or burnout. Set aside a stretch each week when you don't talk about work at all, and let the river inside you flow.
壬戌.ask_next: Has the embankment in your heart been holding back too much lately?

癸亥.title: Rain falling into a boundless sea
癸亥.plain: Rain is Gui Water, and Hai is the river and sea of early winter. Rain falls into the sea, water meeting water, stretching as far as you can see with no edge in sight. You have strong intuition and a rich imagination, you are sensitive, and you can pick up on feelings others leave unsaid. You are accepting and gentle, you get along with all kinds of people, and you adapt well to change. Your inner world is vast, with many thoughts and feelings flowing through it. But when there is too much water, boundaries blur. Other people's emotions flow in, you rise and fall with them, and sometimes you can't tell which feelings are your own.
癸亥.love: In love, you are gentle and accepting, and you are good at caring for your partner's feelings. You easily take their emotions as your own, and when they're unhappy, you feel low too. Practice caring for them while keeping hold of your own mood.
癸亥.work: You suit work that needs imagination and sensitivity, such as creative work, counseling, community management, design, and travel. You understand people well. Watch for having too many directions. Pick one goal so the water has somewhere to go.
癸亥.watch: You are easily carried away by other people's emotions and end up tired yourself. Leave a little time alone each day, return to your own feelings, and sort out which moods are yours.
癸亥.ask_next: The feeling you've had lately: is it yours, or someone else's?

howto: In BaZi, strength is about how much support the Day Master (the stem of the day pillar, which is you) gets across the whole chart. The traditional support-and-restrain method usually looks at three things. First is the month branch: the branch of your birth month stands for the element in season. If it matches the Day Master or helps it, that's called in season, and this counts for the most. Second is the Earthly Branches: it looks at the stems hidden in the four branches and how many match the Day Master or generate it. That's called rooted, which is like asking whether the Day Master has roots. Third is the Heavenly Stems: it counts how many helpers such as Friend, Rob Wealth, Direct Resource and Indirect Resource appear among the other stems. That's called supported. Taken together, if more forces help you, the chart leans strong; if more drain you, it leans weak; if the two sides are about even, it is balanced. A strong chart likes to put its strength out into the world, and a weak chart likes to be fed and supported. This is the view of the support-and-restrain method. Other schools, such as seasonal adjustment and structure, may see it differently, so take this as one angle for understanding yourself.
intro: BaZi pairs the year, month, day and hour you were born with a set of Heavenly Stem and Earthly Branch, arranged into Four Pillars, eight characters in all. Each character carries an element, and they support and restrain one another to form a chart that is yours. From it you can see the Day Master, the essence of who you are. The Ten Gods show how you relate to talent, resources, pressure and learning. The balance and strength of the five elements show what kind of rhythm tends to go more smoothly for you. The luck pillars and annual pillars show where the focus falls in each ten years and each year. Many people don't know what time they were born, and that's fine: with just the year, month and day, you can get three pillars (year, month and day). The Day Master, month branch and most of the Ten Gods can still be read, and only the hour pillar is left blank for now. BaZi doesn't hand you a verdict. It's a map to help you see yourself more clearly.

faq.q: What if I don't know my birth hour?
faq.a: That's fine. BaZi can start with three pillars: year, month and day are all there, and so are the Day Master, month branch and most of the Ten Gods. Without the hour pillar, part of the strength reading is missing, and what relates to later life and children is harder to see. Once you learn the approximate hour, just add it and redo the chart.

faq.q: What's the difference between early Zi hour and late Zi hour?
faq.a: The Zi hour runs from 23:00 to 01:00. The common approach counts the next day as soon as 23:00 passes, and the day pillar changes with it. This is called changing the day at the start of Zi. The other view is that the "late Zi hour," from 23:00 to midnight, doesn't change the day: the day pillar stays on the current day, and the hour pillar's stem is worked out from the next day's Zi hour. For people born in this one hour, the day pillar differs between the two methods, so you can compare both.

faq.q: What is true solar time? Should I turn it on?
faq.a: Clock time is standardized by time zone, but where the sun actually is differs with your longitude. Add the changing speed of Earth's orbit through the year, and the two can differ by ten-plus minutes. True solar time is the time with that gap worked back in. The hour pillar is based on the sun's position, so we suggest leaving it on. It makes the biggest difference for people born near the edge between two hours.

faq.q: Why do the Chinese zodiac sign and the BaZi year pillar change at Start of Spring?
faq.a: BaZi uses a solar-term calendar, in which the year begins at Start of Spring, not on the first day of the first Chinese lunar month. So the year pillar and the Chinese zodiac sign both change at the exact moment of Start of Spring. If you were born between late January and early February, after the Chinese lunar New Year but before Start of Spring, your year pillar and zodiac sign count as the previous year. Conversely, if Start of Spring comes before the New Year, it counts as the new year.

faq.q: Why is my chart different from other sites?
faq.a: Most of the time it's a difference in method. Three are most common. Whether true solar time is used affects the hour pillar. Whether the day changes at 23:00 or the late Zi hour doesn't change it affects the day pillar. And how precisely the moment of a solar term is counted can shift the year or month pillar by one for people born around Start of Spring or the day a month changes. Set these to match and the results usually line up.

faq.q: What if one of the five elements is missing?
faq.a: You don't need to make up for it. BaZi looks at overall balance, and a missing element doesn't mean you lack something. Sometimes it even makes the chart simpler. What really matters is the Day Master's strength and how well the whole chart flows. That element may also be hidden in the Earthly Branches without showing on the surface. Understanding the rhythm that suits you is more practical than rushing to add a character.

faq.q: What is a luck pillar? At what age do they begin?
faq.a: A luck pillar is a ten-year stretch of life rhythm. Stems and branches are laid out forward or backward from the month pillar, showing where the focus of those ten years lies. Whether it runs forward or backward depends on the yin or yang of the year stem and on gender. The age when luck pillars begin is calculated from the number of days between your birth and the nearest solar term before or after. It differs for everyone: some begin at one or two years old, others not until eight or nine.

faq.q: How is BaZi different from Zi Wei Dou Shu?
faq.a: Both use your birth time, but they look at it differently. BaZi uses the Heavenly Stems, Earthly Branches and five elements to read the Day Master's strength and the Ten Gods, and it can chart three pillars even if you don't know your birth hour. Zi Wei Dou Shu places stars into twelve palaces and reads separate areas through the Life Palace, spouse palace, career palace and so on, and it needs your birth hour. You can think of BaZi as a map of the overall structure and Zi Wei as a map of each area of life.
